newsitem.title: CANADA: More than 50,000 protest government cuts in Toronto.
newsitem.headline: More than 50,000 protest government cuts in Toronto.

text.p: More than 50,000 demonstrators marched through the streets of Toronto and converged on the Ontario legislature on Saturday to protest deep budget cuts by the province's Conservative government.

Organized by major labor unions, the demonstration followed mass picketing on Friday that shut the transit system in Canada's largest city and disrupted businesses, government offices and factories for the day. Transit service was back to normal on Saturday.

Preliminary police and media estimates put the number of marchers on Saturday at 50,000 to 70,000 people and said the crowd swelled to about 100,000 for the afternoon rally at the legislature. Organizers, who had expected at least 200,000 to turn out, said about 100,000 participated in the parade and up to 300,000 gathered at the legislature.

Labor leaders and social activists urged the government of Conservative Ontario Premier Mike Harris to retreat from its budget-cutting policies. "Quit throwing people out of work if your agenda is about creating jobs," said Canadian Auto Workers union president Buzz Hargrove.

The march stopped in front of the downtown convention center where the provincial Conservative Party, including the premier, was holding its annual convention. The crowd chanted: "Hey Mike, hey Harris, we'll shut you down like Paris," referring to a general strike in the French capital last week that closed government offices and schools, grounded flights and hampered rail travel.

The Toronto march was largely peaceful but about 15 demonstrators threw rocks at the convention center. Police and parade marshalls quickly quelled the outburst and no damage or arrests were reported.

The demonstration drew factory workers, teachers, firefighters, civil servants, nurses and other citizens from around the province, many arriving by chartered buses. Police closed off downtown streets for about two hours as the marchers traveled from a park near the shores of Lake Ontario to Queen's Park, the site of the legislature.

The protesters waved placards and chanted slogans. The mood was almost festive as clowns, acrobats, folk dancers and drummers joined the throng. Entertainers including Canadian folk singer Bruce Cockburn performed at the rally.
"I'm down here because I don't like what is going on in this province politically," Cockburn told Reuters.

The two "Days of Action" in Toronto followed similar, smaller protests in four other Ontario cities earlier this year. The demonstrators are outraged at Ontario Premier Mike Harris' plans to cut spending by C$8 billion (US$5.9 billion) to wipe out a big budget deficit by the turn of the century.

Dubbed "Newt of the North", in reference to Republican U.S. House Speaker Newt Gingrich, Harris came to power in 1995 on the promise of a right-wing revolution in Canada's most-populous province. His Conservative government has revamped labor laws, slashed welfare payments and required recipients to work. It has also announced plans to close hospitals and cut education spending.
